input: What did Snowflake say about consumption trends on its most recent earnings call?

output.answer: On its most recent earnings call — Q2 of fiscal 2027, for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 (results released September 2, 2026) — Snowflake said consumption-driven product revenue accelerated for a third consecutive quarter, rising 37% year over year to $1.49 billion, with strength in both the core data platform and a 'meaningful step-up' in AI revenue. CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy described a 'flywheel effect' in which AI products CoWork and CoCo are driving new workloads, user growth and overall platform consumption, with AI products contributing roughly half of the growth acceleration. Net revenue retention rose to 126% and remaining performance obligations reached $9.0 billion, up 30% year over year. On the strength of these consumption trends, the company raised full-year FY2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% growth) from $5.84 billion (31%), and guided Q3 FY2027 product revenue to $1.588–$1.593 billion (37–38% growth), noting its forecasts continue to rely on observed consumption patterns.
caveats: Figures are from the Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) report; Snowflake's Q3 FY2027 call has not yet occurred as of November 10, 2026, so a newer quarter's results are not yet available.
The split of growth between AI products and the core platform (about half each) is management's characterization on the call, not a separately audited disclosure.
Guidance is forward-looking and based on consumption patterns management observed; actual consumption in the second half of FY2027 may differ.

passages.quote: Snowflake delivered another strong quarter, with product revenue of $1.49 billion, up 37% year-over-year, as Snowflake continues to power the enterprise AI revolution... AI continues to compound our advantages, creating a flywheel effect across the business. CoWork and CoCo are driving transformational outcomes for our customers, while fueling rapid adoption, user growth, new workloads, and overall platform consumption.

Q2 marks our third consecutive quarter of product revenue growth acceleration, driven by strength in both our core data platform and a meaningful step-up in AI revenue... we are raising our full-year product revenue growth guidance to 36% year-over-year.
passages.publisher: Snowflake (Business Wire press release, Brian Robins, CFO)

passages.quote: For the fiscal third quarter, Robins guided product revenues to $1.588 billion-$1.593 billion or 37-38% growth. He said forecasts continue to rely on observed consumption patterns rather than a changed methodology.
Robins added that fiscal second-quarter product revenues rose 37% year over year, marking a third straight quarter of acceleration, with strength across both the core data platform and AI revenues.
Product revenue grew 37% from a year earlier to $1.49 billion, marking the third consecutive quarter of acceleration.

key_facts.fact: Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) product revenue was $1.49 billion, up 37% year over year — the third consecutive quarter of product revenue growth acceleration, driven by strength in both the core data platform and a meaningful step-up in AI revenue.
Net revenue retention rate was 126% and remaining performance obligations were $9.00 billion, up 30% year over year, as of July 31, 2026.
Snowflake raised full-year FY2027 product revenue guidance to $6,070 million (36% year-over-year growth), up from prior guidance of $5,840 million (31% growth).
Q3 FY2027 guidance: product revenue of $1,588–$1,593 million, representing 37–38% year-over-year growth.
AI adoption metrics cited: CoCo surpassed 9,100 accounts (adding more than 2,000 in the quarter) and CoWork expanded to 5,800 accounts; the company added 692 net new customers, up 32% year over year.
828 customers had trailing 12-month product revenue greater than $1 million, up 27% year over year; 829 Forbes Global 2000 customers.

On the call, CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said AI products contributed approximately half of the growth acceleration, with core products and faster migrations supplying the rest; CFO Brian Robins noted product revenue rose 37% year over year with strength across both the core data platform and AI revenues.

CFO Brian Robins said Q3 forecasts continue to rely on observed consumption patterns rather than a changed methodology, and the company raised FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5% while guiding non-GAAP product gross margin to 74% due to the higher mix of fast-growing AI workloads.

Growth accelerated by 7 percentage points in just two quarters, after Snowflake ended the prior fiscal year at 30% product revenue growth; shares jumped about 22% after hours on the results and raised outlook.
